input.summary: Descriptive pilot proposal for the claim that adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions. No source hash is available (the paper SHA-256 is null); the owner has requested that one be invented, which is not permitted. The packet contains no filled design fields, so a complete pilot cannot be compiled. Three clarifying questions are raised before a full proposal can be drafted.
clarification_questions: What is the actual SHA-256 hash of the paper or dataset you want to use as the input source? A hash cannot be invented — please supply the real identifier before a runnable pilot can be compiled.

What specific TCP flow parameters should be held fixed (e.g., flow size in bytes, number of parallel flows, bottleneck bandwidth, queue discipline) so that the emulated bottleneck conditions can be fully specified in the configuration?

What resource budget (maximum wall-clock seconds, maximum number of replications, and any cost ceiling in USD) is available for this pilot, and should the runner be emulated-netem-v1 or another supported runner?

proposal.problem: The claim asserts that a 20 ms one-way (or round-trip — directionality is unresolved) emulated delay changes TCP flow completion time under a fixed bottleneck, but no source hash, input files, or design parameters are available to anchor a reproducible pilot.
proposal.question: Under the specified fixed emulated bottleneck, what is the observed difference in TCP flow completion time between a 0 ms baseline condition and a 20 ms added-delay condition?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions are anticipated: (1) baseline — fixed bottleneck bandwidth with 0 ms added delay; (2) treatment — identical bottleneck with 20 ms added delay. One-way versus round-trip placement of the delay is unresolved and must be specified by the owner.
proposal.related_work: The source citation is listed as a synthetic networking paper for development evaluation; no full text or SHA-256 is available, so no related-work citations can be verified or reproduced here.
proposal.alternatives: Alternative explanations for any observed difference include queue build-up artifacts from the emulator, TCP slow-start interactions with the added RTT, and measurement-tool timing resolution limits; these are proposed mechanisms, not established facts.
proposal.design: A descriptive within-emulator comparison of TCP flow completion time across the two delay conditions, with replications to characterize observed variability. Exact flow size, bottleneck bandwidth, queue discipline, and TCP variant remain unspecified and must be supplied before the design can be locked.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: TCP flow completion time (units to be confirmed — milliseconds or seconds). Secondary: per-replication observed throughput (Mbps) if available from the chosen runner.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck bandwidth, queue size, TCP variant, flow size, and number of parallel flows must be held constant across conditions; specific values are not yet known.
proposal.inputs: No input files or verified SHA-256 hashes have been supplied. The paper SHA-256 is null and cannot be invented. Input identity and integrity cannot be established until the owner provides real source identifiers.
proposal.limitations: The source hash is null and cannot be invented; no full text is available; all design parameters (flow size, bandwidth, queue discipline, delay directionality, TCP variant) are unspecified. Simulation results cannot establish real-world performance or causality.
